title: ALVEARE: a Domain-Specific Framework for Regular Expressions
problem: Regular expression matching requires massive data analysis with high data dependency, leading to long computational times and high energy consumption. Current RE engines either sacrifice performance for runtime flexibility and broad operator support, or are fixed high-performance accelerators with limited functionality.
motivation: Regular expression matching is critical for diverse applications ranging from proteomics to computer security that require processing massive heterogeneous datastreams.
method: ALVEARE combines a Domain-Specific Language with an embedded Domain-Specific Architecture. Regular expressions are translated into flexible executables through a RISC-based Instruction Set Architecture capable of expressing simple to advanced primitives. A speculation-based microarchitecture executes benchmarks efficiently by leveraging prediction and speculative execution techniques.
key_novelty: A flexible RISC-based ISA specifically designed for RE pattern matching combined with a speculation-based microarchitecture that achieves both domain-specific performance and broad operator support without sacrificing either.
contributions: Domain-Specific Language for translating regular expressions into flexible executable form
RISC-based Instruction Set Architecture for expressing simple to advanced RE primitives
Speculation-based microarchitecture for efficient RE execution
34× speedup and 57× energy efficiency improvements over RE2 and Bluefield DPU 2
